correctness.summary: Two-pointer pair sum computes s = a[l] + a[r] as int + int into an int; with large in-range int values the sum overflows, corrupting the < / > comparisons and skipping valid pairs (or matching wrong ones).
correctness.triggeringInput: k=2, sorted a = {1000000000, 1100000000, 2000000000}, n=3, target=2100000000. The valid pair (1000000000,1100000000)=2100000000 exists, but s=a[0]+a[2]=3000000000 overflows to a negative int < target, so l advances past index 1 and the pair is missed. Returns 0 instead of 1.
correctness.rootCause: int s = a[l] + a[r] overflows for sums exceeding int.MaxValue even when each element and the target are representable ints. The wrapped (negative) sum makes the monotone two-pointer comparison move the wrong pointer.
correctness.suggestedFix: Compute the sum in a wider type, e.g. long s = (long)a[l] + a[r]; and compare against (long)target. Same pattern needed throughout the two-pointer comparisons.

correctness.summary: FourSum computes s = a[i]+a[j]+a[l]+a[r] as a 4-way int addition; in-range int values overflow the int accumulator, breaking the two-pointer comparison and giving wrong counts.
correctness.triggeringInput: n=4, sorted a = {500000000, 600000000, 700000000, 800000000}, target=2600000000 is not representable, but even for representable targets: a={1,2,3,2000000000}? Concretely a={600000000,700000000,800000000,900000000}, target sum of all four = 3000000000 overflows int to negative, so s < target falsely and the quadruple summing to a representable target is mis-handled. E.g. target=2100000000 with a={300000000,400000000,500000000,900000000}: pair sums overflow when combined, l/r move incorrectly and the valid quadruple is missed.
correctness.rootCause: int s = a[i] + a[j] + a[l] + a[r] overflows because four ints near 1e9 exceed int.MaxValue; the wrapped value corrupts the s<target / s>target branch and the pointer advancement.
correctness.suggestedFix: Accumulate in long: long s = (long)a[i] + a[j] + a[l] + a[r]; compare to (long)target.

correctness.summary: On a match the two-pointer does count++; l++; r-- once, which undercounts the number of index pairs when the array contains duplicate values; it counts at most one pair per distinct (value-from-left, value-from-right) boundary rather than all qualifying index pairs.
correctness.triggeringInput: k=2, sorted a = {1,1,1,1}, n=4, target=2. There are C(4,2)=6 index pairs summing to 2, but the method returns 2 (matches at (l=0,r=3) then (l=1,r=2)).
correctness.rootCause: When a[l]+a[r]==target and there are runs of equal values, the correct count is (number of equal lefts) * (number of equal rights), or C(run,2) when both runs coincide. The single count++; l++; r-- only registers one pair and collapses the duplicate block, so the multiplicity of equal elements is lost.
correctness.suggestedFix: On a match, count the length of the equal run at l (cl) and at r (cr); if a[l]==a[r] add cl*(cl-1)/2 and break, else add cl*cr and advance l by cl and r by cr. (FourSum has the same duplicate-undercount issue in its inner two-pointer.)

perf.summary: Hoist partial sums a[i] and a[i]+a[j] out of the two-pointer inner loop so the hot test is a single add.
perf.currentCost: The innermost while recomputes 's = a[i] + a[j] + a[l] + a[r]' fully each step, redundantly re-reading a[i] and a[j] (loop-invariant for the inner while) and re-adding them every iteration.
perf.proposedChange: Before the j-loop body's while, compute 'int ai = a[i];' (outside j-loop) and 'int aij = ai + a[j];'. Inner test becomes 's = aij + a[l] + a[r];'.
perf.rationale: Removes two redundant memory loads and one add from each two-pointer step (the hottest loop, O(n^2) outer with O(n) inner). Shorter dependency chain and fewer loads improve throughput; a[i] hoist also lets it stay in a register across the whole j/while nest.
perf.risk: None: a[i], a[j] are invariant within the inner while; same arithmetic, same count. Assumes sorted input as the algorithm already requires.

perf.summary: Count(...,k,...) only handles k==2 and silently returns 0 for all other k — misleading API; split into TwoSumCount or guard/document.
perf.currentCost: The 'k' parameter and the 'if (k == 2)' branch imply general k-sum support but every k != 2 returns 0 with no signal, a correctness/discoverability trap. The branch on k is also dead overhead on the hot path.
perf.proposedChange: Rename to 'TwoSumCount(int* a, int n, int target)' dropping the k parameter (matching the concrete behavior and the FourSum naming convention), or keep k but follow the Try* convention to indicate unsupported k. Removes the per-call k branch.
perf.rationale: Improves API honesty/discoverability and removes a dead branch; aligns with the existing FourSum naming so callers know exactly what is supported.
perf.risk: Signature change — breaking for callers passing k. Pure ergonomics; numeric behavior for k==2 unchanged.
